newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Bomb rocks government office building in Bogota.
newsitem.headline: Bomb rocks government office building in Bogota.

text.p: A small bomb exploded late on Thursday in a government office building where Colombia's foreign minister was scheduled to give a speech, but police said no casualties or serious damages were reported.
The bomb exploded in a bathroom of the Hemeroteca Nacional, an ornate building on the west end of the capital where a two-day forum on the Non-Aligned Movement opened on Wednesday.
"It wasn't very powerful," a police spokeswoman said.

President Ernesto Samper, who is chairman of the 113-nation Non-Aligned Movement, was originally scheduled to address the closing session of the two-day forum. But Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia was named as a last-minute replacement so that Samper could pay an official visit to the southwest city of Cali instead.
The police spokesowman said Mejia had not yet arrived at the government building, which houses decades worth of newspaper files, when the blast occurred at about 7 p.m. local time (midnight GMT).

There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the bomb but police blamed drug traffickers opposed to lifting Colombia's constitutional ban on extradition for a powerful car bomb discovered early on Tuesday in Cali.
